question:
Select the word segment that substitutes (replaces) the bracketed word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully. Select the option 'no correction required' if the sentence is correct as given.

At last Godfrey (turning his head against her), and their eyes met, dwelling in that meeting without any movement on either side.
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"turning"** means to move or cause to move in a circular direction wholly or partly around an axis or point. (मोड़ना)

 
 
• **Example: **He was turning the doorknob slowly to avoid making any noise.
 
 
 
• **"Turned"** is the past tense of "turn", which implies that the action has already been completed. (मुड़ा हुआ)
 
 
• **Example: **She turned her head when she heard her name.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: no correction required** (कोई सुधार आवश्यक नहीं): This option suggests that the original sentence is correct as it is.

 
 
• **Example:** He was content with the final draft and felt no correction was required.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: turning his head for their** (अपना सिर उनके लिए मोड़ना): This is grammatically incorrect and doesn't fit the context of the sentence.
 
 
• **Example:** The phrase "turning his head for their" doesn't make sense in the given context.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: turn his head along** (साथ में अपना सिर घुमाना): This is also grammatically incorrect and does not fit the context.
 
 
• **Example:** The phrase "turn his head along" is awkward and unclear in meaning.

The correct answer is: **Option 3.**
